description.narrative:
The overall goal of the WE4F 2.0 fund is to increase climate resilience and security of food and water systems in 9 countries across the MENA region through the tailored support of innovative and impactful private sector firms.
Specific objectives include:
- Support of up to 30 SMEs over the life of program, emphasizing businesses that can drive job creation and sustainability in local value chains via regional calls.
- Support of up to 30 rapidly growing early-stage innovative businesses i.e. Scale-ups, in sectors mentioned above, over the life of the program via regional calls.
- a Dedicated track for Syria, Algeria, and Palestine: to select up to 10 firms in each of Algeria, Palestine, and Syria, a total of 30 additional firms, which will be selected via 2 dedicated calls for innovations, with a support period ranging between 12 and 18 months.
- Enhance growth opportunities for targeted Scale-ups and SMEs by addressing systemic and immediate enabling environment challenges through strategic partnerships and tailored interventions. Systemic Enabling Environment (EE) Support will focus on broad-scale, collaborative efforts that tackle structural barriers across sectors, while Direct EE Support will address specific innovator needs through quick, high-impact solutions.
WE4F 2.0 is a challenge fund, as such and as defined by Sida, is a financing mechanism using competition (regional calls) to identify and support innovative solutions addressing the specific challenge set out by the WE4F 2.0 goal. The WE4F 2.0 aims to identify innovations for development impact and intends to engage new actors, contributing to both as financiers and implementers, which can include the mobilization of private capital. The calls of proposals/regional calls will be done through a transparent selection and clearly pre-determined criteria. And expecting a cost-risk sharing with the innovators in the form of match funding. This challenge fund methodology will be used irrespective to the context.
In summary by the end of the intervention the total number of firms that will be supported is:
Track 1 / SMEs: Egypt Lebanon Morocco Tunisia Jordan Iraq: 30-40 firms
Track 2 / Scale-ups Egypt Lebanon Morocco Tunisia Jordan Iraq: 20-30 firms
Track 3 / MSMEs Syria, Algeria, Palestine: 30 firms
Track 4, Syria dedicated call: 30 firms

Stödet syftar till att skala upp innovativa och effektiva lokala företag i nio MENA-länder (Marocko, Algeriet, Tunisien, Egypten, Palestina, Jordanien, Libanon, Irak och Syrien) genom att stödja miljömässigt hållbara lokala innovationer som syftar till att förbättra energi- och vatteneffektiviteten inom den lokala jordbrukssektorn och öka inkomsterna, särskilt för kvinnor och fattiga människor där.
